question.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.

current_example.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{ \mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14158419/assets/ba163a30e7df678b17206c3e720218233fec52f609568d2ec21bbb4ddb7db759.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S} \: \mathbf{x} = A(A^T\!A)^{-1}\!A^T\,\mathbf{x}.
$$

In our case, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14158419/assets/db9f490e120cc5aa1cfa05cff8dd6430d27ae029c0a889e52e40d23a817c1ea4.svg)
Therefore, we get the following projection: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}27 & 9 \\ 9 & 27\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{72}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $\mathbf{x}$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $\mathbf{x}$ and $\textrm{proj}_S \mathbf{x}.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $\mathbf{x}$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to $\textrm{proj}_S \mathbf{x}.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14158419/assets/d22a3c6cadeae2230d20d554eb578a5581e13d155025fa669d6010a1e25a4881.svg)

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{(-1)}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}\cdot \sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta = \arccos\left( \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}2\right)= \dfrac\pi 4,
$$

which is already an acute angle, as desired.
